page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography flags like AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place the n4-standard-8 primarily in the average tier for general compute tasks. It achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11489.89. Memory bandwidth is measured at 530.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 61.33 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, the instance exhibits notable performance bottlenecks in memory-intensive and multi-threaded decompression workloads; its PassMark memory score falls into the bottom 25% at 1809.35, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is similarly weak at 36.22 GB/sec. Additionally, while prompt processing for a medium 7B LLM model reaches 49.59 tokens/sec, text generation on the same model is poor, yielding only 6.31 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource profile suitable for mainstream enterprise workloads without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and standard memory density, it is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight single-threaded or small-model machine learning tasks. It is less suitable for memory-bound applications, heavy multi-threaded decompression, or large-scale LLM text generation.
